title: One script, five variations: each changes one thing
hook: One script, five variations. Each variation changes exactly one thing.
caption:
One script, five variations. Each variation changes exactly one thing.

The easy way to brief variations is to change everything at once: new opening, new creator, new music, new ask. Five ads come back, one does better, and nobody can say which change did it.

Keep the script fixed. Change one of five things per variation: the opening, the person, the setting, the format or the ask. Name each variation in the brief and use the same name on the file and the ad.

One caution. The variations have to look different at a glance, or they compete with each other.

The next step is to put these on a calendar. Decoded #11 shows how.
alt_text: Eight-slide carousel in Shrutik Rathod's Brief to Live series. One script, five variations, each changing one thing: the opening, the person, the setting, the format or the ask. One slide shows a Galvor finding: a proven message in a new look got 47% more first-month spend. Other slides compare changing everything with changing one thing, explain naming each variation in the brief, and warn that variations must look different. Last slide asks readers to follow Galvor and read Decoded #11.

slides.headline: One script, *five variations.* Each one changes one thing.
slides.sub: How to brief variations you can learn from.

slides.headline: Change everything and you learn *nothing*
slides.body:
New opening, new creator, new music, new ask. Five ads come back and one does better.

Nobody can say which change did it, so the next brief starts from a guess.

slides.headline: Keep the script. Change *one* thing.
items: Opening — a new first three seconds
Person — a different face says the same lines
Setting — a kitchen instead of a studio
Format — talking to camera instead of a demo

slides.headline: more first-month spend for a *proven message in a new look*
slides.sub: The message stays. The look changes.
slides.source: Source: Galvor analysis · ads launched May–Sep 2026

slides.headline: Five edits or *five tests*
right: Next brief starts from a fact

slides.headline: Name every variation *in the brief*
slides.body:
Opening-problem. Person-commuter. Setting-kitchen.

Use the same name on the file and on the ad, so anyone can read the results without asking what was what.

slides.headline: Variations must *look* different
slides.body:
Near-copies launched together compete with each other.

If two variations look the same at a glance, merge them and make one bolder change.

slides.headline: Brief *one change* at a time
slides.sub: Decoded #11 shows how to turn tests like these into a calendar.

notes:
Reader: a creative or brand manager briefing creator variations (Convert: the next step is Decoded #11, Build a Test Calendar). Shape: how-to. Hook shape: punchy plus context. Written as a method with no personal anecdote, so nothing to confirm beyond Shrutik being happy to put his name to it.
Numbers used: 47% (proven message in a new look got 47% more first-month spend; Galvor analysis of video ads launched May to Sep 2026, Decoded #3), used once in this group. The 'one caution' slide rests on the same analysis (look-alike ads got less first-month spend) and uses no number.
The earlier draft offered a one-page variation brief by comment. That offer is removed because the first comment now points only to Decoded #11. List items use the ' — ' separator the slide template needs.
